Package org.jdesktop.lg3d.displayserver.desktop2d

Class WindowCycler<T>

java.lang.Object
org.jdesktop.lg3d.displayserver.desktop2d.WindowCycler<T>
public final class WindowCycler<T> extends Object
The most-recently-used window list and cycle state machine behind a desktop's window switcher.

This is the pure-logic half: it tracks which application window was used most recently (touch(T)/forget(T)) and, once a cycle session is open, walks a highlight index forward and backward through the MRU-ordered snapshot. It paints nothing and touches no Java 3D, so the cycling behaviour is unit-testable headless; a switcher overlay (the 2D WindowCyclerOverlay, or the native 3D desktop's HUD switcher) renders whatever this exposes.

The class is desktop-agnostic and generic over the window type: the 2D desktop cycles WindowCycler<Desktop2DWindow> while the native 3D desktop cycles WindowCycler<org.jdesktop.lg3d.wg.Frame3D>, so both share one MRU/cycle model instead of each re-inventing it.

A session opens on the first trigger and highlights index 0 (the window that currently has the focus). The first advance() then moves to index 1 — the window the switcher jumps to first — and repeated advances walk the list, wrapping. commit() returns the highlighted window and closes the session; cancel() closes it without selecting anything.

Confined to a single thread (the event dispatch thread on the 2D desktop, the lg3d event thread on the 3D one), like the rest of the switcher.

      public T selected()

    • open

      public boolean open(List<T> present)
      Opens a cycle over present (the windows currently on the desktop), ordered most-recently-used first, and highlights index 0. Returns false, leaving the session closed, when there are fewer than two windows — there is nothing to switch to.

    • ordered

      public List<T> ordered(List<T> present)
      Orders present most-recently-used first: the tracked windows that are still present (most recent leading), then any present window that was never tracked, appended in the given order. The result is a snapshot; it never mutates the MRU history.

    • advance

      public void advance()
      Moves the highlight one window forward, wrapping. No-op when closed.

    • advanceBack

      public void advanceBack()
      Moves the highlight one window backward, wrapping. No-op when closed.

    • commit

      public T commit()
      Returns the highlighted window and closes the session, or null when no session is open. The caller brings the returned window forward.

    • cancel

      public void cancel()
      Closes the session without selecting anything.
